transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what finally got me to come in is my eating has just gotten really strange and off, and it’s been going on for months. It’s not like one normal change where I’m just eating more or less. Some days I barely want anything, like I’ll just pick at a piece of toast and drink coffee and then realize that’s basically all I’ve had. And then other days I’ll find myself in the bakery aisle buying cookies or pastries or whatever, sweets I don’t even really enjoy that much, and I don’t know why I’m doing it exactly.

It feels like my appetite is all turned around, like I can’t trust it. It’s embarrassing to say because it sounds small, maybe, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. It’s actually one of the things that makes me feel most unlike myself, if that makes sense. I used to get really excited about little things, like picking out fabric for quilting squares. I could spend forever matching colors and patterns, laying them out on the table, thinking, “Oh, this one will look nice next to that one.” Now I can look right at my sewing supplies, all the fabric and thread just sitting there, and I feel… nothing much. Or I feel tired of it before I even start.

And bowling night used to be something I looked forward to. Not that I was ever great at it, but I liked the routine of it, seeing people, having a laugh if I threw a terrible ball. Lately, even when I know it’s coming up, I just can’t get myself to care enough to go, or even to miss it properly.

Same with church things, like potlucks. I used to like planning what to bring, checking the calendar, thinking through who might like what. Now I’ll look at the church calendar and it’s like I’m looking at a grocery list for somebody else’s life. I know those things used to matter to me, but I can’t seem to feel it the way I used to.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time lately, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yes… most days, honestly. It’s not always because something happened, that’s the strange part. I can wake up and nothing is technically wrong right then, and it’s still there, like this heavy sad feeling is already sitting on me before I’ve even gotten out of bed.

I’ll go into the kitchen, and it’s a bright enough room, you know, the kind of room that should feel cheerful in the morning. I’ll have the coffee going, and the light coming in, and I know those things used to feel comforting. But lately it’s like the warmth has gone out of everything. I’m standing there doing the same little morning things, and it all feels flat and heavy, like I’m moving through a day that’s already been drained of whatever was supposed to make it feel like a day.

And I keep thinking there should be a reason I can point to, but a lot of the time there isn’t one clear thing. It’s just there.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yes… I do. More than I want to admit, really. It’s this constant feeling that I’ve failed somehow, even when people tell me I haven’t.

Like at church, folks will say, “You’re doing fine,” or they’ll be kind to me, and I can nod and smile, but it doesn’t really settle in. I keep feeling like they’re just saying that to be polite, because what else are they going to say to my face? In my mind, it feels like everybody in Manawa knows I’m not doing what I should, especially with my aunt. Like I’m letting her down somehow, not being enough, not handling things the way a decent person would.

And I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, dramatic maybe. But it feels real when I’m in it. I’ll be at church or even just thinking about going into town, and I get this awful feeling that people are whispering about me, that they all know I’ve become a burden. Like they can see it on me before I even open my mouth. Even if nobody says anything unkind, I still feel sure they’re thinking it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, like not being able to fall asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than you'd like and not being able to get back to sleep?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I mean… I sleep, at least I think I do, but I haven’t been keeping track of it in any careful way. Some nights feel longer than others, and I’ll lie there thinking, “Have I been asleep or just lying here?” but I don’t know if that counts as trouble sleeping the way you mean.

I can’t say for certain that I’m waking up too early or anything like that. I just know mornings don’t feel very restful lately, but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with the actual sleep part. Maybe if I paid more attention I could tell you better.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual or that you’re lacking energy, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. It’s not even like I can say, “Well, I did a lot yesterday, so of course I’m tired.” It happens even on the quieter days.

There are mornings when my aunt hasn’t called out during the night, so technically I should be rested, you know? I’ll think, “All right, I got through the night, I slept enough,” but then by the time breakfast is over I already feel worn down. Not just sleepy exactly, more like my body and my mind have both been used up before the day has really started.

Something simple like carrying laundry feels like it takes more out of me than it should. Or making phone calls — even if it’s just one or two calls, nothing complicated — I’ll sit there afterward feeling like I had to climb a hill to do it. And I know those aren’t big things. I know people do them every day without making a whole production out of it. But lately they feel heavier than they ought to.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight or appetite lately, like losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yes… that’s actually part of why I came in, because my eating has gotten all turned around, and it’s been like that for months now. It’s not just one bad week or something I can explain by being busy.

Some days I barely want anything. I’ll have toast and coffee and sort of pick at it, like I know I ought to eat but nothing sounds right, and I don’t really feel hungry in the normal way. Then other days it goes the other direction, and I’ll find myself standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets — cookies or pastries or whatever’s there — and the strange thing is I don’t even really enjoy them. It’s not like a treat. It’s more like I’m doing it because I feel pulled to, or because I don’t know what else to do with myself.

As far as weight, I haven’t been carefully tracking it, so I don’t want to say the wrong thing. But the appetite part, yes, that has definitely changed. It feels uneven and not like me.
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving more slowly than usual, or that you’re moving more slowly in a way that other people might notice?

Yes… I think so. I didn’t really notice it at first because, you know, when you’re the one doing it, it just feels like you’re getting through the day the way you can. But other people have started saying things.

At the grocery store, more than once, someone has asked me if my hip is bothering me, because I guess I’m walking so slowly down the aisles. And it’s embarrassing, because nothing exactly happened to my hip. I’m not limping from an injury or anything. I just move slow, like I have to think through every step, or like my body doesn’t quite start when I tell it to.

And it’s not only walking. At meetings, if someone asks me a simple question, I’ll take too long to answer. I can feel everyone waiting, and I know it should be easy — just say yes or no, or give the little answer they’re asking for — but my mind sort of drags before the words come out. Then I get more self-conscious, which probably makes it worse.

So yes, I guess other people have noticed it. I don’t like admitting that, but they have.
Have you lost your appetite or noticed that food doesn’t taste the same to you lately?

Yes… I mean, it’s hard to explain because it hasn’t been the same every day. That’s part of what bothers me. My eating has just gotten all turned around for months now.

Some mornings I’ll make toast and coffee because that’s what I’m supposed to do, you know, and then I’ll just sort of pick at it. I’ll take a bite or two and it’s like… nothing is appealing. It’s not that I’m trying not to eat. I just don’t feel drawn to food the way I used to.

And then other days it’s almost the opposite. I’ll end up standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets — cookies or pastries or whatever — and even then I don’t really enjoy them. It doesn’t feel like, “Oh, this tastes so good.” It’s more like I’m eating because I don’t know what else to do, or because something in me is pulling me toward it. So yes, my appetite has definitely changed. Food doesn’t feel normal to me lately.
